predecessors.note: 'The state was established in 1808 in the wake of the partition between the rulers of the royal house of Kedah' and the territory went to a cadet branch of the royal family (Setul page). The sultanate-of-kedah dossier records the 1808 loss to this slug.

land.text: Satun province, to which the kingdom's borders 'were largely inherited'

successors.note: 'The Siamese decided to discontinue the Malay kingship system in Setul' in 1916; the territory became a Siamese province governed by an official from Bangkok, whose borders 'were largely inherited' by the present Thai province of Satun.

correction.text: Satun province, to which the kingdom's borders 'were largely inherited'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row). The page gives no area or boundary: 'Its borders were largely inherited to its successive province, the present-day Satun, Thailand', so the shape is the modern province of Satun. The sultanate-of-kedah dossier draws the same land as a Cliopatria Kedah intersection with Satun.

region.text: Satun province, to which the kingdom's borders 'were largely inherited'

ledger.note: 1808: Setul is founded out of Kedah. 'The state was established in 1808 in the wake of the partition between the rulers of the royal house of Kedah'; 'the partition witnessed the territory being seceded to the cadet branch of the royal family'; first ruler Tunku Bisnu (infobox 1809-1843). The page names Siam as having appointed Tunku Bisnu, and gives the borders only as the later province of Satun.

region.text: Satun province, to which the kingdom's borders 'were largely inherited'

ledger.note: 1843: the partition of Kedah is ratified and Setul becomes one of four dominions pledging loyalty to the Siamese crown. 'The partition was ratified by 1843'; each dominion sent Bunga Mas tribute to Bangkok (the page's wording, paraphrased). The page does not call Setul a vassal in so many words; it says Siam 'perceived Kedah as their vassal'.

region.text: Satun province, to which the kingdom's borders 'were largely inherited'

ledger.note: 1892: Setul is returned to Kedah. 'In 1892, Setul was returned to Kedah'; Kedahan sovereignty was then 'gradually eroded by the Siamese' and by 1902 'it was evident that Ku Din held full-autonomous power over Setul against Kedah'. The sultanate-of-kedah dossier records this as a gain of the land in 1892; the Setul page has the kingdom and its ruler (Tunku Baharuddin, 1897-1916) surviving, so it is recorded here as a subordination, not as an end.

region.text: Satun province, to which the kingdom's borders 'were largely inherited'

ledger.note: 1909: Kedah's jurisdiction over Setul ends. 'The Kedahan jurisdiction in Setul was officially ended by 1909 in wake of the Anglo-Siamese Treaty.' The treaty page gives signature on 10 March 1909, transfer of Kelantan, Terengganu, Kedah, Perlis and adjacent islands to Britain, ratifications exchanged on 9 July 1909, and does not mention Setul; the Setul page gives only 'by 1909'. Pairs the 1892 vassal_start.

region.text: Satun province, to which the kingdom's borders 'were largely inherited'

ledger.note: 1916: Siam takes Setul under direct rule. 'The Siamese decided to discontinue the Malay kingship system in Setul'; the page says the 'sovereignty of the kingdom effectively ended in 1916, following the dissolution by the Siamese government'. Pairs the 1843 vassal_start.

region.text: Satun province, to which the kingdom's borders 'were largely inherited'

ledger.note: 1916: the kingdom of Setul ends. 'The sovereignty of the kingdom effectively ended in 1916, following the dissolution by the Siamese government'; its last ruler Tunku Baharuddin bin Ku Meh reigned 1897-1916; Setul became a Siamese province (Satun).

certainty.note: The page gives no boundary; Satun province is the inherited border.

sources.title: Setul Mambang Segara
sources.note: Founded 1808 in the partition of Kedah; ratified 1843; returned to Kedah in 1892; Kedahan jurisdiction ended by 1909; dissolved by Siam in 1916; borders inherited by Satun; rulers Tunku Bisnu (1809-1843) to Tunku Baharuddin (1897-1916).

sources.title: Anglo-Siamese Treaty of 1909
sources.note: Signed 10 March 1909; transferred Kelantan, Terengganu, Kedah, Perlis and adjacent islands; ratifications exchanged 9 July 1909; Setul not mentioned.

notes: Written 2026-10-24 by the se-03-x additions batch; the slug is the counterpart named twice in the sultanate-of-kedah dossier. Two pages opened. Unsettled: (1) the Setul page and the Kedah dossier disagree about 1892: the Kedah dossier calls it a reunification and a territorial gain for Kedah (1892) and a loss to Siam (July 1909); the Setul page keeps the kingdom, its ruler and a Siamese-influenced autonomy to 1916, so this dossier records vassal_start and vassal_end with Kedah as counterpart, not a loss (the orchestrator should reconcile: either side may carry the land); (2) the Kedah dossier dates the creation to 1808 (a Kedah page) and a reviewer's Siamese invasion page to 1811; the Setul page says 1808; (3) 1843: the page gives 'ratified by 1843' for the partition and the four dominions; the Siamese suzerainty is read from that, not from a dated sentence; (4) no capital, area or rulers beyond the first and last are on the page; (5) wars: the page names the 'Perang Musuh Berbisik' (War of the whispering enemies) of 1833 and a Phuket expedition of 1878 (260 people sent), without belligerents or lands; none is recorded; (6) the Monthon Syburi map of 1900 places Setul in Siam's administration; no event; (7) the 1916 end is the page's 'effectively ended in 1916', not a dated act. Gazetteer: Satun (admin1, Thailand) resolves already.
